newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down, Telefonica resists undertow.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down, Telefonica resists undertow.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Tuesday as most companies saw profit-taking while benchmark Telefonica del Peru resisted the undertow, brokers said.
The market was expected to dip again Wednesday as investors were seen continuing to take profits after last week's sharp price rises, they added.
Tuesday the General Index fell 0.34 percent to 1,603.0 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.81 percent to 2,131.3 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

Telefonica bucked the general downward trend Tuesday because its rises the previous week had been more circumspect than those of most other shares and there were still "buy" orders for the telecom, brokers said.
Telefonica rose 1.76 percent to 5.77 soles on volume of 2.56 million shares.

"Only Telefonica showed any life in the market because there were many orders to buy," said Carlos Guimeth of local brokerage Multivalores. "This is a hangover from the recent announcement that interest rates in the United States would not be going up."
Last week's strong gains on the market were prompted by news that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not hike interest rates.
Amongst leaders Tuesday, the biggest losers were those stocks that had risen most sharply in the recent bull run.

Chocolate maker D'Onofrio DON.LM fell 4.32 percent to 1.33 soles on volume of 281,000 shares. The country's largest brewery, Backus y Johnston, dropped 2.77 percent to 2.81 soles on 1.0 million shares, while its sister company, Compania Nacional de Cerveza, closed down 3.38 percent at 1.43 soles on 320,000 shares.
In a total of 2,462 operations, 29 stocks rose, 30 fell and 41 were stable in volume of 36.8 million ($14.6 million).
